articles.summary: Patient apps are often framed as convenience. But in African healthcare, the deeper constraint is that patients don’t “exist” consistently across the system. Fragmented identity means records don’t travel, benefits don’t travel, and care keeps resetting. This piece makes the case for a reliable patient identity layer as the real unlock for portability across facilities and networks.
articles.title: The Case for Patient Identity in Africa

articles.summary: Healthcare in many African markets does not fail only because care is unavailable. It often fails because care is hard to complete. Patients may find a provider, but booking is inconsistent. They may see a clinician, but next steps are unclear. Results arrive late or get lost. Payments feel opaque.
